channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealnd Dollar weakens after China PMI miss as the US Dollar rebounds
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5860 on Friday, down 0.33% on the day, as investors react to another deterioration in Chinese business activity.

item.title: Euro: Range seen around mid‑1.15s against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s FX team notes EUR/USD is drifting toward 1.15 after a Fed‑driven rally, with euro area CPI broadly in line with expectations and French data briefly lifting the Euro. Rate expectations are stabilizing, with about 42 bps of tightening priced by December.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens against British Pound amid intervention speculation
item.description: GBP/JPY extends its slide on Friday as suspected intervention by Japanese authorities rattles the FX market and lifts the Yen across the board, pushing the cross further away from the multi-year high of 219.16 touched earlier this month.

item.title: Japanese Yen surges amid hawkish BoJ
item.description: USD/JPY trades sharply lower near the 159.50 area on Friday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens following intervention by Japanese authorities and a relatively hawkish Bank of Japan (BoJ) policy announcement.

item.title: Canada: Growth outpaces forecasts – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economists Abbey Xu and Nathan Janzen note that Canadian Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose 0.3% in May, with an advance estimate of 0.2% for June, indicating a solid second-quarter rebound after winter stagnation.

item.title: United States: Broad-based Q2 GDP strength beyond AI – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Eli Nir and Oscar Munoz highlight that Q2 United States (US) Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth slowed to 1.5% q/q AR, but underlying private domestic final purchases accelerated to 3.9%.

item.title: Aluminium: Tightness points to higher prices – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke highlights that China’s July trade data will be key for base metals, especially Aluminium. Chinese Aluminium output in H1 exceeded the official cap, suggesting production may ease later this year.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk and hawkish BoJ support Yen – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that USD/JPY briefly fell about five big figures to 158.00 on suspected Japanese intervention before rebounding near 161.00 and then dropping again.

item.title: Gold declines as firmer US Dollar, hawkish Fed outlook weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges lower on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) stabilizes following the previous day’s sharp sell-off, while hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations remain a key headwind for the non-yielding metal.

item.title: India: RBI hold expectations shape policy outlook – ING
item.description: ING economists Deepali Bhargava and Lynn Song expect the Reserve Bank of India to keep the repo rate at 5.25% this week. They note that while June headline inflation rose on higher fuel prices, core inflation remains below target.

item.title: Euro slips back below 1.1500 as US Dollar recovers
item.description: The Euro (EUR) weakens against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday as short-covering in the Greenback following the previous day’s sharp sell-off pushes EUR/USD back below 1.1500. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1488, easing from the six-week high of 1.1537 touched on Thursday.

item.title: China: Policy support balances weak PMIs – UOB
item.description: UOB economist Ho Woei Chen highlights that China’s July CFLP PMIs slipped into contraction, with both manufacturing and non-manufacturing gauges signaling broad-based weakness in activity. The report notes particularly soft industrial output and services, while construction also declined.

item.title: Canadian Dollar shrugs off upbeat GDP as US Dollar stages a comeback
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.4045 on Friday at the time of writing, recovering from a two-week low hit on Thursday at 1.3991.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ patience keeps wide trading range – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities notes the Bank of Japan (BoJ) left its policy rate at 1% with an 8–1 vote, as Governor Ueda delivered notably hawkish remarks. Despite this, the Japanese Yen (JPY) reaction was muted, and the TD forecasts the next 25 bps hike only in December.

item.title: Breaking: Canada's GDP expanded by 0.3% MoM in May
item.description: Canada’s economy cooled a tad in May. Indeed, the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 0.3%, adding to the previous month's 0.6% expansion (revised from 0.5%), according to data released by Statistics Canada.

item.title: Gold: Reduced Fed hike bets support prices - Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch notes that gold briefly traded above USD 4,100 after the Fed meeting as markets pared back expectations of further rate hikes. Fed funds futures nevertheless continue to imply additional tightening, while persistent inflation is keeping those expectations alive.

item.title: British Pound: Softer BoE stance seen weighing on Sterling – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that the Bank of England (BoE) left rates at 3.75% with a 6–3 vote, while Governor Andrew Bailey pushed back against expectations of an imminent hike.

item.title: Euro: ECB September hike still base case – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists highlight that Euro area Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) inflation rose to 2.9% y/y in July, with core inflation at 2.5% and services inflation at 3.3%, indicating only limited evidence of meaningful second-round effects.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy credibility and intervention dynamics – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that the Japanese Yen (JPY) entered the latest Bank of Japan (BoJ) decision and suspected intervention with weak flow momentum and lighter positioning, even as investors remained net long JPY and net short USD/JPY.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD remains under pressure as bond yields, US Dollar rebound
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is down 1.7% to near $58.00 during the European trading session on Friday. The white metal continues to decline throughout the day as United States (US) Treasury Yields have bounced back amid fears that inflationary pressures will remain elevated.

item.title: Brent: Conflict risks keep prices elevated – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke and colleagues highlight that Brent remains volatile as Middle East tensions and shipping disruptions through key chokepoints constrain supply.

item.title: Japanese Yen dips back to 160.00 against the US Dollar as post-BoJ gains fade
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) posts moderate losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with the USD/JPY pair trading just above 160.00 at the time of writing, after whipsawing within a rough 240-pip range between 158.60 and 161.00 earlier on the day.

item.title: US Dollar Index: DXY seen returning to 96.00–100.00 range – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the Dollar stabilized after a sharp sell-off linked to suspected USD/JPY intervention, but argues the broader USD rally since May has likely ended, with US Dollar Index (DXY) expected to move back into a 96.00–100.00 range.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds firm despite weak Chinese data, fading RBA rate hike bets
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7030 at the time of writing on Friday, little changed on the day after Thursday's strong rally.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Balanced growth supports CAD – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect Canadian real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to rise by 0.2% m/m in May, exceeding the flash estimate and extending April’s 0.5% gain. They highlight balanced growth across goods and services, with manufacturing, existing home sales and retail trade all contributing.

item.title: Indian Rupee sets for bets weekly close in four months
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends the week-long rally against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday.

item.title: Experts agree: The US Dollar rally might have found serious headwinds
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) attempts to cling above the 100.00 psychological level on Friday after a nearly 1.5% selloff in the previous three days, as the Federal Reserve's (Fed) lack of forward guidance at Wednesday's monetary policy meeting raised concerns that the bank might fail on its commitment

item.title: US Dollar: Post-Fed losses extend as positioning unwinds – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes the Dollar’s post-FOMC selloff has accelerated, with DXY briefly dipping below 100.0 and returning to levels seen after Kevin Warsh’s June press conference. He highlights stretched net-long USD positioning versus G9 and large EUR/USD shorts.

item.title: Euro rebounds vs Yen as BoJ rate hold, Eurozone inflation support
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 184.00 on Friday, stabilizing after the sharp volatility seen on Thursday. The cross plunged to near 182.00 from around 187.00, losing almost 500 pips within minutes after what appears to have been another intervention by Japanese authorities in the foreign exchange market.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Wide range trading outlook – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Alex Loo notes that despite Governor Ueda’s hawkish tone, the Japanese Yen reaction was muted and the BoJ kept its policy rate at 1%.
